executiveSummary: GM0331's 2025 identity, boundary, centre, 14,800 residents, 14 neighbourhoods and five BAG places are coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Lopik is an elongated rural municipality in the subsiding peat-and-clay Lopikerwaard, bounded by the Lek and dependent on a dense polder-water system. The canonical river preset reports 1.524692 m depth-like inundation at both T+24 and T+72, 6,557 then 7,094 affected people-equivalent and exact lifeline losses without a selected Lek hydrograph/datum, defence reach, breach or overflow pathway, inundation footprint, arrival or recession. Defence evidence is reach-specific: the completed Salmsteke work covers 2 km only; Jaarsveld-Klaphek preparation is delayed and Salmsteke-Schoonhoven remains in plan development. Neither project status proves present failure nor an all-clear. Pluvial T+24 reports 0.545762 m and 2,179 affected without rainfall, catchments, groundwater, sewer state, receiving-water level, maalstop or pump operation. HDSR says polder pumps generally remove about 13 mm/day, De Koekoek drains three quarters of the Lopikerwaard and may need emergency power, while the same structure can reverse mode during drought to feed the 5.6 m3/s KWA route. Those are conditional capabilities and design context, not live state or guaranteed resilience. A 242-point water register, provider territories, one grid-planning sample, antennas, schools and current Cabauw weather/air observations remain context, not topology or capacity. The transport graph reduces access to N204 plus two non-additive N210 edges, omitting local/dike-road dependencies and the seasonal active-mode Lek ferry; 88 scheduled stop areas do not establish service. Exact hazard, service and first-72-hour recovery claims require source gating or clear synthetic labelling; missing, empty, stale or out-of-horizon data remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0331 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement, safety-region and statistics inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs uniquely identify GM0331 as Lopik in Utrecht and Veiligheidsregio Utrecht, with 14,800 residents, density 196/km², 19.4% aged 65 or older and 1,635 one-person households. The reference point [4.948418914356529,51.989657722499246] is inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Fourteen neighbourhoods in one district sum to 14,790 residents, ten below the municipal total (-0.068%); published households sum to 5,920 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 2,875. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 14,800 without rewriting observations.

Five active BAG places—Benschop, Jaarsveld, Lopik, Lopikerkapel and Polsbroek—are contained. BRT contributes eleven woonkern/deelkern/buurtschap labels including Cabauw, Graaf, Uitweg, Willige Langerak and Zevender. BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0.

District-heating and public-charging fields are missing in all 14 neighbourhoods. Publisher null, suppression or non-applicability remains NoData, not zero. Annual residents omit incident-time visitors, commuters, pupils, agricultural workers, care users and ferry/recreation users.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Municipal sewer policy, climate stress-test context and regional flood-awareness map
evidenceSources.edition: Gemeentelijk Rioleringsplan Lopik 2022–2026 and current regional flood-map page inspected 3 September 2026; blanket page/PDF reuse licence not stated
supports: The official 2022–2026 plan governs sewerage and urban water, explicitly linking the system to public health, water nuisance and climate adaptation. It records a regional 2018 stress test covering water nuisance, heat, drought and water safety. Policy and modelled stress are planning evidence, not current event state.

Municipal technical requirements describe an extensive rural municipality with varied gravity, pressure and vacuum sewer systems plus pumps/telemetry. This supports distinct local dependencies but exposes neither operational telemetry, spare capacity, backup endurance nor failure state.

The municipality's regional flood map at https://www.lopik.nl/regionale-overstromingskaart states that flooding remains possible despite protection and was prepared with HDSR, neighbouring water authorities, Rijkswaterstaat, Province Utrecht and VRU for awareness/self-safety. Map v2.0 is preparedness context, not a selected event footprint or forecast.
The correct local water model must distinguish Lek/primary defence, regional-kade/boezem, polder/wetering/groundwater, sewer/pluvial and drought/freshwater modes.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Severe-water-nuisance mechanisms, maalstop, pump failure and De Koekoek emergency context
evidenceSources.edition: Current authority page inspected 3 September 2026; update cadence and blanket page reuse licence not stated
supports: HDSR identifies heavy/prolonged rain, pump failure, maalstop, blocked watercourse and dike breach as distinct causes. In its polder area, pumps generally remove about 13 mm/day and can run at full capacity during heavy rain; excess rainfall and unavailable ditch/boezem storage can cause nuisance.

If boezem levels threaten regional defences, HDSR can stop or reduce pumping, accepting polder-ditch overflow to reduce a different failure risk. Rijkswaterstaat can also impose constraints affecting the Hollandsche IJssel. These are conditional authority decisions, not automatic model transitions.

Pumps can fail from electricity loss or defect. HDSR may deploy tractor- or generator-driven emergency pumps and says some important pumps have diesel backup for a time; it specifically says De Koekoek drains three quarters of the Lopikerwaard.

Capability language does not establish which backup exists at each asset, fuel/endurance, crew/connection time, current pump mode, discharge, available storage, receiving-water level or action completion.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Lopikerwaard peat-polder drainage and completed KWA freshwater route
evidenceSources.edition: Current KWA route and western-water-system pages inspected 3 September 2026; project reported complete in summer 2025; blanket page reuse licence not stated
supports: The western water-system page at https://www.hdsr.nl/werk/droge-voeten/drie-regio%27/watersysteem-west/ describes low peat polders, continuing subsidence and continuous managed drainage; De Koekoek normally discharges much of the Lopikerwaard to the Lek.

During drought, De Koekoek can instead admit Lek freshwater through the Lopikerwaard to Keulevaart and the Gekanaliseerde Hollandsche IJssel. The KWA route was enlarged to a stated robust design capacity of 5.6 m³/s and the construction project was completed in summer 2025.
Normal drainage and drought water-supply are opposite controlled modes at the same location. A static point/function or undifferentiated drainage percentage cannot represent both.
The 5.6 m³/s design value is not a live flow, available reserve, local flood-discharge capacity, power-independent capacity or guaranteed first-72-hour service.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Reach-specific Sterke Lekdijk completion and current project status
evidenceSources.edition: Salmsteke completion published 10 December 2024; Jaarsveld-Klaphek delay published 20 July 2026; Salmsteke-Schoonhoven current plan page inspected 3 September 2026; blanket page reuse licence not stated
supports: The completed Salmsteke reach runs only from Rolafweg Zuid to Jaarsveld and is 2 km long. It was handed over on 9 December 2024. That completion must not be generalized to all Lekdijk in or serving Lopik.

For Jaarsveld-Klaphek, HDSR's definitive project decision covers a 9.2 km reach with more than 4 km intended for strengthening. At https://www.hdsr.nl/buurt/sterke-lekdijk/jaarsveld-klaphek/nieuws/%40236020/uitvoering-dijkversterking-jaarsveld/ HDSR reported on 20 July 2026 that its planned 1 October preparatory start was no longer achievable because no contract was awarded; a new schedule was not known.

Salmsteke-Schoonhoven is an 8 km reach whose current page at https://www.hdsr.nl/buurt/sterke-lekdijk/salmsteke-schoonhove/ remains in the 2022–2027 plan-development phase, with realization planned for 2027–2030; HDSR identifies piping, inward macro-stability and peat-foundation subsidence as design issues.

A strengthening need or delayed project is not evidence of an incident or failure. Conversely, one completed reach is not an all-clear. Operational use needs exact reach/chainage, inspection/alert state, failure mode, issue/valid time and uncertainty.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — N210/N204 corridor, seasonal Lek ferry and waterway/access semantics
evidenceSources.edition: Province page updated 20 July 2026; municipal ferry page and Rijkswaterstaat Lek overview inspected 3 September 2026; NWB light geometry dated 1 August 2026; blanket web-page reuse licences not stated
supports: The province treats N210 Schoonhoven–Nieuwegein as one long corridor split into seven works sections. Completed 2022–2025 works and planned Lopik-Oost construction for 2028–2029 are not present restrictions; future works must not be applied early.

NWB exposes N204 toward Montfoort and two GM0331 N210 border edges toward Krimpenerwaard and IJsselstein. Both N210 edges share NWB-road-210 and are consecutive/series, not two additive escape routes or observed emergency throughput.

The municipality identifies at https://www.lopik.nl/recreatie-en-toerisme-0 the seasonal foot/bicycle ferry De Overkant between Lopik/Jaarsveld and Ameide. It is a separate active-mode connection omitted by the road graph; seasonal timetable, weather, crew and incident status are required before any evacuation use is assumed.

Rijkswaterstaat identifies at https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/water/vaarwegenoverzicht/lek the Lek as a Rhine distributary and principal navigation route. Static waterway identity and zero bounded NDW records do not establish local water level, navigability, bridge/ferry/road status or open access.

evidenceSources.publisher: KNMI / RIVM / Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Timestamped Cabauw observations and public asset/provider/service context
evidenceSources.edition: Public-context snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; HWH CC BY-SA 4.0, Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain, DUO CC BY version unspecified, RIVM v1.1 CC0; KNMI/NBNL/RDI reuse terms remain those of their individual source metadata
supports: HWH assigns 242 realized point assets using the 2025 non-generalized boundary: 211 weirs, 23 surface-water pumps, seven sewer pumps and one wastewater-treatment point. Twenty-two capacity fields are non-null, but numbers lack a displayed comparable unit/connectivity model; De Koekoek's register function says discharge while authority evidence also establishes drought intake mode.

The Cabauw KNMI observation at 2026-09-02 23:30Z recorded 17.6 °C, gust 6.27 m/s and zero hourly rain, and Utrecht carried an explicit no-warning publication. Those are time-scoped observations/warnings, not validation of a synthetic exercise or a 72-hour all-clear.
Cabauw-Wielsekade's RIVM interval ending 17:00Z reported PM2.5 4.09 µg/m³. A single station/interval is not a plume, municipality-wide exposure or future wildfire-smoke forecast.

A centre-point territory query to https://public.geodata.mijnaansluiting.nl/geoserver/mijnaansluiting_open/ows identifies Stedin electricity/gas, Vitens water and Ziggo media; drainage is empty. One Stedin planning sample reports 27 MW existing and 46.4 MW required withdrawal, queues and projects. Territories and planning values are not live topology, outage, loading, spare capacity or restoration.

RDI returns 30 antenna sites and DUO nine education sites. There are no assigned Waterinfo observations/forecasts, bounded NDW situations, public-service points, acute hospitals or seismic events. Empty/absent coverage remains Unknown/NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public warning, evacuation and first-72-hour preparedness guidance
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal page and national Denk vooruit guidance inspected 3 September 2026; blanket municipal page reuse licence not stated
supports: Lopik lists siren/NL-Alert and official information channels, shelter-in-place guidance, evacuation preparation, neighbour checks and following the police-designated route. It says institutions arrange special transport for their own needy people, elderly residents or pupils where applicable.

The page itself notes sirens are concentrated in settlements above 1,000 residents and are sparse in small villages, countryside and recreation areas. A listed channel is not proof of alert issuance, geographic reach, receipt, comprehension or completion.

National Denk vooruit guidance at https://www.rijksoverheid.nl/actueel/nieuws/2025/11/17/minister-van-oosten-presenteert-informatieboekje-bereid-je-voor-op-een-noodsituatie asks households to prepare for 72 hours without water, electricity or internet. It is guidance, not a measured Lopik stock, equal self-reliance or restoration promise.

No reviewed public source provides a Lopik-specific, resource-backed T0–T+72 action ledger for warnings, water/defence controls, evacuation/reception, mobility, care, emergency utilities, welfare, supply or repair.
